# Proposal: Reimagining Our Museum Experience

## A Plan for Thoughtful Renewal on a Limited Budget

---

## Introduction

Our museum holds a treasured collection that tells the story of this community, but the way we present it has not changed in a generation. Visitors walk through rooms crowded with objects, often with little explanation of how these items fit into daily life. This proposal outlines a practical plan to renew our exhibits around five core commitments: showing fewer objects with richer context, protecting fragile pieces through rotation, gathering stories from residents, improving physical accessibility, and using technology selectively rather than universally. Every element of this plan is designed to work within our limited budget and to accommodate the realities of volunteer availability.

# Proposal: Reimagining Our Galleries for the Whole Community

## Introduction

Our museum holds a treasured collection that tells the story of this town, but the way we present it no longer serves our visitors as well as it could. Crowded display cases, minimal interpretation, and physical layouts that assume able-bodied visitors have all limited our reach. This proposal outlines a practical, affordable plan to redesign our permanent galleries around a simple principle: fewer objects, richer stories, and access for everyone. It acknowledges our constraints honestly—a limited budget and a volunteer corps with uneven availability—and explains where we can act now and where we must compromise.

## The Problem We Are Solving

Walk through our galleries today and you will see dozens of objects per room, each with a small label naming the object and its donor. Visitors move quickly, overwhelmed and under-informed. Fragile textiles and paper items sit under lights for months at a time, slowly deteriorating. There is nowhere to sit in most rooms. Residents who lived the history we display walk past objects they could explain, because we have never asked them to.
